│                        │     │                   927028a5bab 
│                        │     ├ Title           : MessagePack for Python: Out-of-bounds read / crash on
│                        │     │                   Unpacker reuse after a caught error 
│                        │     ├ Description     : ### Impact
│                        │     │                   
│                        │     │                   If the Unpacker is used repeatedly after an error occurs,
│                        │     │                   the process may crash with a SEGV.
│                        │     │                   If the Unpacker is used repeatedly to unpack untrusted input
│                        │     │                    from external sources, it may be vulnerable to a DoS
│                        │     │                   attack.
│                        │     │                   ### Patches
│                        │     │                   v1.2.1
│                        │     │                   ### Workarounds
│                        │     │                   Users should create a new Unpacker instead of reusing the
│                        │     │                   same Unpacker after an error occurs.
│                        │     │                   Applying the above patch can prevent SEGV, but reusing the
│                        │     │                   Streaming Unpacker after it has encountered an error will
│                        │     │                   not yield correct data. If an error occurs during Streaming
│                        │     │                   Unpacking, the Stream and Streaming Unpacker should be
│                        │     │                   discarded.
│                        │     │                   Therefore, this is not just a workaround but the correct
│                        │     │                   solution. The above patch only prevents crashes from
│                        │     │                   incorrect usage.

│                        │     ├ Title           : setuptools: Path Traversal Vulnerability in setuptools
│                        │     │                   PackageIndex 
│                        │     ├ Description     : setuptools is a package that allows users to download,
│                        │     │                   build, install, upgrade, and uninstall Python packages. A
│                        │     │                   path traversal vulnerability in `PackageIndex` is present in
│                        │     │                    setuptools prior to version 78.1.1. An attacker would be
│                        │     │                   allowed to write files to arbitrary locations on the
│                        │     │                   filesystem with the permissions of the process running the
│                        │     │                   Python code, which could escalate to remote code execution
│                        │     │                   depending on the context. Version 78.1.1 fixes the issue.

│                        │     ├ Title           : setuptools: setuptools: MANIFEST.in exclusion bypass in
│                        │     │                   sdist via Unicode normalization collision (NFC/NFD) 
│                        │     ├ Description     : setuptools is a package that allows users to download,
│                        │     │                   build, install, upgrade, and uninstall Python packages.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 83.0.0, FileList applied MANIFEST.in exclude,
│                        │     │                   global-exclude, recursive-exclude, and prune directives by
│                        │     │                   matching compiled glob patterns against on-disk file names
│                        │     │                   without Unicode normalization, so on macOS APFS or HFS+ an
│                        │     │                   NFD file name could bypass an NFC exclusion rule and be
│                        │     │                   packed into a source distribution. This issue is fixed in
│                        │     │                   version 83.0.0.

│                        │     │                   92d56163818 
│                        │     ├ Title           : urllib3: urllib3: Traffic interception via HTTPS proxy TLS
│                        │     │                   configuration override 
│                        │     ├ Description     : urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. From 1.26.0
│                        │     │                   until 2.8.0, the proxy_ssl_context, proxy_assert_hostname,
│                        │     │                   proxy_assert_fingerprint, ssl_context, cert_reqs,
│                        │     │                   verify_mode, use_forwarding_for_https=True, and CERT_NONE
│                        │     │                   configuration paths fail to remain separated because
│                        │     │                   target-server TLS settings are incorrectly applied to the
│                        │     │                   HTTPS proxy connection. The trigger is that an application
│                        │     │                   uses an HTTPS proxy and configures target-server TLS
│                        │     │                   settings that must remain separate from the proxy TLS
│                        │     │                   handshake, including HTTPS forwarding with target-specific
│                        │     │                   identity or credentials. Applying cert_reqs=CERT_NONE can
│                        │     │                   overwrite proxy_ssl_context.verify_mode in place, and the
│                        │     │                   mutation persists so later connections reusing the same
│                        │     │                   context may connect to the HTTPS proxy without certificate
│                        │     │                   verification. The attack mechanism is that an attacker
│                        │     │                   intercepts and impersonates the HTTPS proxy after the
│                        │     │                   effective proxy policy accepts the attacker's certificate.
│                        │     │                   The impact is that the attacker can observe or modify
│                        │     │                   forwarded traffic or receive a target TLS client
│                        │     │                   certificate, while CONNECT tunneling still preserves the
│                        │     │                   separate end-to-end target TLS connection. This issue is
│                        │     │                   fixed in version 2.8.0.

│                        │     │                   5c59b9c5819 
│                        │     ├ Title           : urllib3: urllib3: Denial of Service via unbounded memory
│                        │     │                   allocation in chunk parser 
│                        │     ├ Description     : urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. From 1.10.3
│                        │     │                   until 2.8.0, the HTTPResponse.read_chunked and
│                        │     │                   HTTPResponse.stream methods can allocate unbounded memory
│                        │     │                   because the streaming chunk parser buffers the chunk-size
│                        │     │                   field until newline or EOF without a length bound. The
│                        │     │                   trigger is that a malicious server returns
│                        │     │                   Transfer-Encoding: chunked followed by a very long run of
│                        │     │                   bytes without a newline. The attack mechanism is that a
│                        │     │                   malicious HTTP server sends a very long unterminated
│                        │     │                   chunk-size line. The impact is that unbounded memory
│                        │     │                   allocation can exhaust the client process. This issue is
│                        │     │                   fixed in version 2.8.0.

│                              │                   f03aa7f529e 
│                              ├ Title           : urllib3: urllib3: Denial of Service via infinite loop during
│                              │                    chunked Deflate decoding 
│                              ├ Description     : urllib3 is an HTTP client library for Python. From 2.6.2
│                              │                   until 2.8.0, HTTPResponse.stream and
│                              │                   HTTPResponse.read_chunked can enter an infinite loop because
│                              │                    the Deflate decoder retains trailing bytes as unconsumed
│                              │                   input after reaching end-of-stream and repeatedly decodes
│                              │                   them without progress. The issue occurs when an untrusted
│                              │                   server sends a chunked Deflate response whose decoded body
│                              │                   exceeds a positive finite chunk size and whose encoded body
│                              │                   has trailing bytes, specifically a response with
│                              │                   Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Encoding: deflate,
│                              │                   content decoding enabled, and the positive finite amt=N
│                              │                   streaming chunk size. The attack mechanism is that a
│                              │                   malicious server returns a compressed chunked response with
│                              │                   trailing bytes after the Deflate stream. The impact is
│                              │                   excessive CPU usage and a request that does not complete,
│                              │                   and network read timeouts do not interrupt the loop because
│                              │                   no further socket read occurs. This issue is fixed in
│                              │                   version 2.8.0.

│                        │      │                   ccadca87c578 
│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      │                   333536aeb567 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                        │      ├ Title           : crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   multiple ECH outer extension references 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted
│                        │      │                   under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a
│                        │      │                   well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in
│                        │      │                    the server process by specifying multiple references. We
│                        │      │                   now reject these as malformed and curb the memory
│                        │      │                   amplification vector as a result.

│                        │      │                   6694313a0845 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via
│                        │      │                    desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a
│                        │      │                   non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the
│                        │      │                   connection without framing after the request headers. If
│                        │      │                   the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx
│                        │      │                   keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to
│                        │      │                   the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a
│                        │      │                   request body, the server may interpret the trailing body
│                        │      │                   bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the
│                        │      │                   connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized
│                        │      │                   and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the
│                        │      │                   response to the injected request. In reverse proxies
│                        │      │                   (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT
│                        │      │                   requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to
│                        │      │                   cross-user response poisoning.

│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      │                   44e8bcabdbb9 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via
│                        │      │                   improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an
│                        │      │                   HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the
│                        │      │                   connection, the server improperly continues to read and
│                        │      │                   serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to
│                        │      │                    an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel,
│                        │      │                   the server should not treat the connection as continuing to
│                        │      │                    contain HTTP. The impact of this misbehavior is mostly
│                        │      │                   limited to potential request smuggling, where an
│                        │      │                   intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to
│                        │      │                   be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP.

│                        │      ├ Title           : html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via
│                        │      │                   consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive
│                        │      │                   expressions, the context tracking state was not properly
│                        │      │                   reset upon entering a new expression. We now ensure that
│                        │      │                   template-literal expression entries correctly reset context
│                        │      │                    variables so all subsequent regular expression literals
│                        │      │                   are accurately recognized and escaped.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                               │                   junction handling 
│                               ├ Description     : On Windows, when the target of Root.Mkdir or Root.MkdirAll
│                               │                   is a junction pointing to an empty location, the operation

│                        │      │                   8cedfb59ef0e 
│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      │                   a3f7bc30f9e4 
│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      │                   cfc2dd10fba0 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                        │      ├ Title           : crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   multiple ECH outer extension references 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted
│                        │      │                   under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a
│                        │      │                   well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in
│                        │      │                    the server process by specifying multiple references. We
│                        │      │                   now reject these as malformed and curb the memory
│                        │      │                   amplification vector as a result.

│                        │      │                   18d449d27036 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via
│                        │      │                    desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a
│                        │      │                   non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the
│                        │      │                   connection without framing after the request headers. If
│                        │      │                   the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx
│                        │      │                   keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to
│                        │      │                   the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a
│                        │      │                   request body, the server may interpret the trailing body
│                        │      │                   bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the
│                        │      │                   connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized
│                        │      │                   and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the
│                        │      │                   response to the injected request. In reverse proxies
│                        │      │                   (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT
│                        │      │                   requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to
│                        │      │                   cross-user response poisoning.

│                        │      │                   0cc878cdc623 
│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      │                   ce0dfa5f469a 
│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      │                   6503f2ec954f 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via
│                        │      │                   improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an
│                        │      │                   HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the
│                        │      │                   connection, the server improperly continues to read and
│                        │      │                   serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to
│                        │      │                    an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel,
│                        │      │                   the server should not treat the connection as continuing to
│                        │      │                    contain HTTP. The impact of this misbehavior is mostly
│                        │      │                   limited to potential request smuggling, where an
│                        │      │                   intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to
│                        │      │                   be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │      ├ Title           : html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via
│                        │      │                   consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive
│                        │      │                   expressions, the context tracking state was not properly
│                        │      │                   reset upon entering a new expression. We now ensure that
│                        │      │                   template-literal expression entries correctly reset context
│                        │      │                    variables so all subsequent regular expression literals
│                        │      │                   are accurately recognized and escaped.

│                        │      │                   e6c8b8f64011 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of
│                        │     │                   Service via nil pointer dereference in response validation[
│                        │     │                   m 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.146.0, openapi3filter.ValidateResponse passes a
│                        │     │                   nil response header schema to decodeValue when an OpenAPI
│                        │     │                   document declares the header with content instead of schema.
│                        │     │                    The document passes validation, but every response
│                        │     │                   validation for the affected operation dereferences the nil
│                        │     │                   schema and panics even when the response does not contain
│                        │     │                   the declared header. Applications that ingest an untrusted
│                        │     │                   specification can expose this as remote availability impact,
│                        │     │                    while applications using only trusted local specifications
│                        │     │                   still crash when the affected operation is exercised. This
│                        │     │                   issue is fixed in version 0.146.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Authentication
│                        │     │                   bypass via URL path decoding discrepancy 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From
│                        │     │                    0.144.0 until 0.147.0, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler
│                        │     │                   validates an operation selected from decoded URL.Path while
│                        │     │                   a downstream gorilla/mux router configured with
│                        │     │                   UseEncodedPath can dispatch a different operation selected
│                        │     │                   from URL.RawPath. When a public exact route and a protected
│                        │     │                   parameterized route use the same method and overlap after
│                        │     │                   decoding, an unauthenticated remote request containing an
│                        │     │                   encoded path separator can be validated as public and then
│                        │     │                   dispatched to the protected handler without invoking the
│                        │     │                   configured AuthenticationFunc. The reachable path parameter
│                        │     │                   is constrained to an encoded representation that decodes to
│                        │     │                   the public literal route, and proxies that canonicalize the
│                        │     │                   URI before forwarding prevent this specific mismatch. This
│                        │     │                   issue is fixed in version 0.147.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of
│                        │     │                   Service via improper handling of non-finite numeric values[
│                        │     │                   m 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.148.0, the OpenAPI 3.1 validation path passes
│                        │     │                   YAML NaN and infinity numeric values to
│                        │     │                   santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6.0.2 without applying
│                        │     │                   kin-openapi's existing finite-number guards. A remote
│                        │     │                   unauthenticated client can send an application/yaml or
│                        │     │                   application/x-yaml request body containing .nan, .inf, or
│                        │     │                   -.inf to an operation with a numeric constraint, causing the
│                        │     │                    dependency to create and dereference a nil big.Rat during
│                        │     │                   ValidateRequest. Standard net/http servers recover the panic
│                        │     │                    per connection, while other hosts or application goroutines
│                        │     │                    may terminate the process. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │     │                   0.148.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of
│                        │     │                   Service via nil-pointer dereference in request decoding 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From
│                        │     │                    0.136.0 until 0.149.0, three openapi3filter decoder paths
│                        │     │                   that were missed by the fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 lack a
│                        │     │                   nil-items guard for legal OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas. An
│                        │     │                   unauthenticated remote client can trigger a deterministic
│                        │     │                   nil-pointer panic through an array query parameter, a
│                        │     │                   deepObject query parameter containing an array property, or
│                        │     │                   an application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body whose
│                        │     │                   array property appears inside an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf
│                        │     │                   subschema. The query and composed-body paths reach
│                        │     │                   urlValuesDecoder.parseArray, while the deepObject path
│                        │     │                   reaches buildResObj, and all pass a nil items schema into
│                        │     │                   code that dereferences it. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │     │                   0.149.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of
│                        │     │                   Service via unbounded recursion during schema validation 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.149.0, runtime request, response, and direct
│                        │     │                   schema validation lacks cycle detection when an allOf,
│                        │     │                   anyOf, or oneOf chain refers back to an ancestor schema,
│                        │     │                   even though loading and document validation accept the
│                        │     │                   circular reference. A request or response that reaches the
│                        │     │                   affected schema causes unbounded recursion in
│                        │     │                   Schema.visitJSON or openapi3filter.decodeValue and exhausts
│                        │     │                   the Go goroutine stack. The resulting fatal stack overflow
│                        │     │                   cannot be caught with recover and terminates the entire
│                        │     │                   process, including unrelated requests. This issue is fixed
│                        │     │                   in version 0.149.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of
│                        │     │                   Service via unsupported HTTP methods on static paths 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.145.0, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler uses the
│                        │     │                   routers/legacy router, which passes an unsupported or
│                        │     │                   non-canonical HTTP method for an existing static path to
│                        │     │                   openapi3.PathItem.GetOperation. The default branch of
│                        │     │                   GetOperation panics before authentication runs, so an
│                        │     │                   unauthenticated remote client can repeatedly send methods
│                        │     │                   such as PROPFIND or lowercase get to abort connections and
│                        │     │                   generate stack-trace log growth. The specific panic requires
│                        │     │                    an exact static path; a concrete path matched only by a
│                        │     │                   templated route does not reach the same sink. This issue is
│                        │     │                   fixed in version 0.145.0.

│                        │     ├ Title           : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.145 ... 
│                        │     ├ Description     : kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files.
│                        │     │                   Prior to 0.145.0, openapi3.Loader can dereference a nil
│                        │     │                   SchemaRef.Value while resolving a self-referential
│                        │     │                   additionalProperties JSON Reference such as a schema that
│                        │     │                   points to its own additionalProperties member. Loading an
│                        │     │                   attacker-controlled OpenAPI document through LoadFromData,
│                        │     │                   LoadFromFile, or LoadFromURI reaches resolveComponent before
│                        │     │                    document validation and can panic the loading process.
│                        │     │                   Resolved additionalProperties schemas and ordinary recursive
│                        │     │                    schemas do not take the vulnerable nil-value path. This
│                        │     │                   issue is fixed in version 0.145.0.

│                        │      │                   908b7530f7ce 
│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                        │      ├ Title           : crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   multiple ECH outer extension references 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted
│                        │      │                   under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a
│                        │      │                   well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in
│                        │      │                    the server process by specifying multiple references. We
│                        │      │                   now reject these as malformed and curb the memory
│                        │      │                   amplification vector as a result.

│                        │      │                   82e10d6b5328 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via
│                        │      │                    desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a
│                        │      │                   non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the
│                        │      │                   connection without framing after the request headers. If
│                        │      │                   the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx
│                        │      │                   keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to
│                        │      │                   the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a
│                        │      │                   request body, the server may interpret the trailing body
│                        │      │                   bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the
│                        │      │                   connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized
│                        │      │                   and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the
│                        │      │                   response to the injected request. In reverse proxies
│                        │      │                   (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT
│                        │      │                   requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to
│                        │      │                   cross-user response poisoning.

│                        │      │                   2e864ebb7e57 
│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      │                   c1de4baa8da9 
│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      │                   3824d494bad8 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via
│                        │      │                   improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an
│                        │      │                   HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the
│                        │      │                   connection, the server improperly continues to read and
│                        │      │                   serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to
│                        │      │                    an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel,
│                        │      │                   the server should not treat the connection as continuing to
│                        │      │                    contain HTTP. The impact of this misbehavior is mostly
│                        │      │                   limited to potential request smuggling, where an
│                        │      │                   intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to
│                        │      │                   be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP.

│                        │      ├ Title           : html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via
│                        │      │                   consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive
│                        │      │                   expressions, the context tracking state was not properly
│                        │      │                   reset upon entering a new expression. We now ensure that
│                        │      │                   template-literal expression entries correctly reset context
│                        │      │                    variables so all subsequent regular expression literals
│                        │      │                   are accurately recognized and escaped.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                               ├ Title           : os: golang: golang: Directory traversal via Windows
│                               │                   junction handling 
│                               ├ Description     : On Windows, when the target of Root.Mkdir or Root.MkdirAll
│                               │                   is a junction pointing to an empty location, the operation

│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   concurrent HPACK encoder modification 
│                        │      ├ Description     : HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently
│                        │      │                   modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens
│                        │      │                   because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two
│                        │      │                   goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to
│                        │      │                    encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a
│                        │      │                   client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when
│                        │      │                    handling a SETTINGS frame containing
│                        │      │                   SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious
│                        │      │                    client can repeatedly send a request while changing the
│                        │      │                   header table size to crash the server.

│                        │      ├ Title           : crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via
│                        │      │                   multiple ECH outer extension references 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted
│                        │      │                   under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a
│                        │      │                   well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in
│                        │      │                    the server process by specifying multiple references. We
│                        │      │                   now reject these as malformed and curb the memory
│                        │      │                   amplification vector as a result.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via
│                        │      │                    desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a
│                        │      │                   non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the
│                        │      │                   connection without framing after the request headers. If
│                        │      │                   the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx
│                        │      │                   keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to
│                        │      │                   the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a
│                        │      │                   request body, the server may interpret the trailing body
│                        │      │                   bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the
│                        │      │                   connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized
│                        │      │                   and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the
│                        │      │                   response to the injected request. In reverse proxies
│                        │      │                   (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT
│                        │      │                   requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to
│                        │      │                   cross-user response poisoning.

│                        │      ├ Title           : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internall ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

│                        │      ├ Title           : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related  ... 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling.

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control.
